course: Introduction to the Internet of Things
topic_title: Industrial IoT Protocols: WirelessHART & Short-Range Connectivity

analysis_of_assignment_style.question_format: Multiple Choice Questions (4 options: A, B, C, D)
analysis_of_assignment_style.evaluation_depth: Combination of direct factual recall, component identification, protocol/standard matching, and scenario-based application reasoning.

Medium/Hard (Multi-concept synthesis, scenario reasoning, boundary conditions)

topics.description: HART standards, TDMA timeslots, 2.4 GHz channels, and superframes.

questions.question: According to Week 3 Assignment Question 1, is there a network layer in Wired HART?

options.A: True (There is no network layer in Wired HART)

questions.justification: Wired HART operates directly on physical and data link layers and has no network layer.

questions.question: In the US, at what frequency does Z-Wave operate as tested in Assignment Week 3 Question 2?
questions.justification: Z-Wave operates at 908.42 MHz in the US and 868.42 MHz in Europe.

questions.question: Which medium access technique is used at the MAC layer in WirelessHART to guarantee collision-free transmission?

options.B: TDMA (Time Division Multiple Access) with 10ms timeslots

questions.justification: WirelessHART uses TDMA with 10ms timeslots grouped into superframes.

questions.question: What is the standard channel bandwidth timeslot duration in WirelessHART superframes?
questions.justification: WirelessHART time slots are precisely synchronized to 10ms.

questions.question: Which ISM frequency band is utilized by WirelessHART?
questions.justification: WirelessHART operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM band (using IEEE 802.15.4 radios).

questions.question: Why is Channel 26 removed from usage in WirelessHART networks?

options.A: Because Channel 26 has restricted usage/regulatory limits in certain regions
options.D: Channel 26 is reserved for Bluetooth headsets

questions.justification: Channel 26 is blacklisted/removed due to regional regulatory transmit power restrictions.

questions.question: How does WirelessHART achieve high transmission reliability in harsh industrial noise environments?

options.A: Using channel hopping after every packet transmission combined with channel blacklisting
options.C: Replacing wireless radios with copper wires

questions.justification: Per-packet channel hopping and blacklisting bad channels prevents persistent multipath fading and interference.

questions.question: What network topology is employed at the network layer in WirelessHART?
questions.justification: WirelessHART utilizes a mesh topology where every node can route packets for its neighbors.

questions.question: How many channel frequencies in the 2.4 GHz band are available for WirelessHART transmissions after excluding channel 26?
questions.justification: IEEE 802.15.4 defines 16 channels in 2.4 GHz (channels 11-26). Removing channel 26 leaves 15 usable channels.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of simultaneous packet transmissions supported in a WirelessHART network during a single 10ms timeslot across all available channels?
questions.justification: With 15 available channels, up to 15 different packets can propagate simultaneously in a 10ms timeslot without interference.

topics.description: Blacklisting, hopping, and comparisons with Zigbee/Sub-GHz.

questions.question: According to Assignment Week 3 Question 4, what process removes interference-prone channels from active use?
questions.justification: Channel Blacklisting identifies channels consistently affected by interference and removes them from the hopping sequence.

questions.question: Is Bluetooth technology based on ad-hoc network topology according to Assignment Week 3 Question 10?
questions.justification: Bluetooth is an ad-hoc short-range wireless networking technology (forming piconets/scatternets).

questions.question: Which modulation and encoding are used by Z-Wave?

options.B: GFSK modulation and Manchester / NRZ encoding

questions.justification: Z-Wave utilizes GFSK modulation with FSK/NRZ Manchester encoding.

questions.question: What is the standard data rate of Zigbee operating at 2.4 GHz according to Week 3 Assignment Question 6?
questions.justification: Zigbee operating at 2.4 GHz delivers a raw data rate of 250 kbps.

questions.question: Which channel access mechanism is used by Zigbee at the MAC layer?

options.B: CSMA/CA (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance)

questions.justification: Zigbee uses CSMA/CA for channel access, unlike WirelessHART's TDMA.

questions.question: Compare the MAC layer channel access of WirelessHART and ZigBee. Which statement is correct?

options.A: WirelessHART uses TDMA with per-packet channel hopping; ZigBee uses CSMA/CA and hops only when the entire network hops
options.B: WirelessHART uses CSMA/CD; ZigBee uses TDMA
options.D: ZigBee uses per-packet channel hopping; WirelessHART does not hop

questions.justification: WirelessHART uses TDMA with per-packet hopping; ZigBee uses CSMA/CA without per-packet hopping.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Network Manager in a WirelessHART industrial network?

options.A: It establishes routing tables, assigns TDMA timeslots, and configures superframes centrally
options.C: It converts Python scripts to C++
options.D: It supplies AC power to field instruments

questions.justification: The central Network Manager in WirelessHART configures superframes, routes, and timeslot schedules.

questions.question: How does ISA 100.11a compare with WirelessHART in industrial automation?

options.A: Both are 802.15.4-based industrial standards supporting TDMA and mesh routing, but ISA 100.11a supports multiple messaging sub-protocols including IPv6
options.B: ISA 100.11a is an optical fiber standard

questions.justification: ISA 100.11a and WirelessHART both target industrial mesh automation, but ISA 100.11a offers broader native IPv6 transport integration.

questions.question: What operating range is typical for Near Field Communication (NFC) protocols?
questions.justification: NFC operates over extremely short distances (typically under 4 cm) using 13.56 MHz inductive coupling.

questions.question: How does an active RFID tag differ from a passive RFID tag?

options.A: Active tags contain an internal battery source to power radio transmissions; passive tags harvest energy from the reader's RF field
options.B: Passive tags have batteries; active tags do not

questions.justification: Active RFID tags carry onboard batteries for longer range; passive tags rely on electromagnetic energy harvested from reader signals.

topics.topic_name: Comparative Analysis of Short-Range Wireless Standards
topics.description: Z-Wave, Bluetooth/BLE, NFC, and RFID mechanics.

questions.question: Which wireless short-range protocol is specifically optimized for low-power home automation operating in Sub-1 GHz bands?
questions.justification: Z-Wave is a proprietary Sub-GHz mesh protocol optimized for smart home automation.

questions.question: What protocol layers are defined in ZigBee architecture?

options.A: Physical, MAC, Network, and Application layers built on IEEE 802.15.4

questions.justification: Zigbee defines Network and Application layers on top of IEEE 802.15.4 PHY/MAC layers.

questions.question: Which protocol standard operates at 13.56 MHz for secure contactless payments and pair-and-pay interactions?
questions.justification: NFC operates at 13.56 MHz for ultra-short-range transactions.

questions.question: True or False: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM band and uses frequency-hopping spread spectrum (FHSS).

options.D: Only with optical line of sight

questions.justification: BLE operates in 2.4 GHz ISM band using FHSS across 40 channels.

questions.question: Which component in an RFID system emits radio waves to read data stored on an RFID tag?
questions.justification: An RFID Reader (interrogator) transmits RF power to interrogate RFID tags.

questions.question: Why does operating Z-Wave in Sub-1 GHz frequency bands reduce interference in home environments compared to 2.4 GHz protocols?

options.A: Sub-1 GHz avoids heavy congestion from Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and microwave ovens operating in 2.4 GHz
options.B: Sub-1 GHz signals cannot pass through air
options.D: Sub-1 GHz uses zero transmission power

questions.justification: Sub-GHz bands avoid 2.4 GHz crowding and penetrate walls with lower attenuation.

questions.question: In a Bluetooth piconet, what is the maximum number of active slave devices that can communicate with a single master node simultaneously?
questions.justification: A classic Bluetooth piconet supports 1 master and up to 7 active slave nodes simultaneously.

questions.question: What key advantage does Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) offer over Classic Bluetooth for IoT sensors?

options.A: BLE achieves ultra-low duty cycles and rapid sleep/wake state transitions, reducing energy consumption by orders of magnitude

questions.justification: BLE is designed for short packet bursts with aggressive sleep cycles, allowing multi-year coin-cell battery life.

questions.question: Which industrial standard protocol integrates WirelessHART into unified Field Device Tool (FDT) framework software?
questions.justification: WirelessHART integrates seamlessly with existing HART tools, EDDL, and FDT frameworks.

questions.question: What is the primary trade-off between passive RFID tags and active RFID tags in asset tracking?

options.A: Passive tags are virtually maintenance-free and cheap but have short read range (< 10m); active tags have long range (> 100m) but higher cost and battery limits
options.B: Passive tags require high-capacity lithium batteries
options.C: Active tags cannot store digital memory

questions.justification: Passive tags harvest reader energy (cheap, infinite shelf life, short range); active tags carry batteries (longer range, higher cost).
